  REGULAR MEETING OF THE
  SAN MARINO CITY COUNCIL
  WEDNESDAY, MAY 10, 2023 AT 6:00 PM
  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE
  SAN MARINO, CA 91108

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
adjourned meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@CityofSanMarino.org or by phone at
(626) 300­0705 prior to the meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City will
do it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chou, Council Member Lo, Council Member Shepherd Romey, Vice Mayor
Huang, and Mayor Talt

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the Stoneman
Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.cityofsanmarino.org.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At this
time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda. Pursuant
to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the meeting
agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to place limits on
duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.

CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

This is an opportunity for the City Manager to inform the City Council and the public of any
upcoming events or matters of interest to the community.

MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READINGS

This action permits the City Council to act on ordinances and resolutions without having to
read the entire text of the ordinance or resolution. The title of an ordinance on First
Reading must be read in its entirety. An ordinance on Second Reading does not require
having the title read. However, the City Council may request that an ordinance or resolution
be read in its entirety before taking any action.

  NEW BUSINESS

3.  APPOINTMENT OF MEMBERS TO CITY OF SAN MARINO ADVISORY
  BODIES
  Recommendation: The Council Liaisons for the Design Review Committee recommend
  the Council appointment of two (2) regular members and one (1) alternate member
  to serve two­year terms, each commencing on June 1, 2023, and one (1) alternate
  member to complete the term ending May 31, 2024 (commencing immediately) to the
  Design Review Committee. The Council Liaisons for the Library Board of Trustees
  recommend the Council appointment of one (1) regular member and two (2) alternate
  members to serve three­year terms each commencing on June 1, 2023. If Council
  concurs, the appropriate motions would be: “I move to appoint Christa Lakon and
  Rick Chou as regular members and Suzanne Torgeson as an alternate member of the
  Design Review Committee to serve terms ending May 31, 2025, and to appoint
  Kimberlee Misek as an alternate member of the Design Review Committee to complete
  the term ending May 31, 2024” and “I move to appoint Steve Domier as a regular
  member, and Vivi Wahl and Sandy (Chiao) Wu as alternate members of the Library
  Board of Trustees to serve terms ending May 31, 2026.”

4.  CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT FOR THE MONTH OF MARCH 2023
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file this report. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be: “I
  move to receive and file the Cash and Investment Report for the Month of March
  2023.”

5.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. R­23­15, RESCINDING
  RESOLUTION NO.'S R­21­28 AND R­22­18 TO ELIMINATE THE
  MANDATORY VACCINE MANDATE FOR THE UNREPRESENTED
  EMPLOYEES AND EMPLOYEES REPRESENTED BY THE SMPOA,
  SMFFA, AND MODIFYING THE MOU WITH THE SMCEA
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council adopt Resolution No. R­23­15. If
  Council agrees with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:“I move
  to adopt Resolution No. R­23­15, Rescinding Resolution No.'s R­21­28 and R­22­18 to
  Eliminate the Mandatory Vaccine Mandate for the Unrepresented Employees,
  Employees Represented by the SMPOA and SMFFA, and Modifying the MOU with the
  SMCEA.”

6.  APPROVAL OF AMENDMENTS TO THE AGREEMENTS WITH CRANE

6.  APPROVAL OF AMENDMENTS TO THE AGREEMENTS WITH CRANE
  ARCHITECTURAL GROUP, KELLY SUTHERLIN MCLEOD
  ARCHITECTURE, AND GRIFFIN STRUCTURES; ADDITIONAL
  HAZARDOUS MATERIAL ABATEMENT SERVICES BY VISTA
  ENVIRONMENTAL; AND OF A PROFESSIONAL DESIGN SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH CSI FULLMER FOR THE SAN MARINO
  COMMUNITY CENTER PROJECT
  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve the contract
  amendments, additional hazardous material abatement services, and award a
  professional design services agreement to CSI Fullmer. If the Council concurs, an
  appropriate motion would be: “I move to approve Amendment No. 4 to the
  professional design services agreement with Crane Architectural Group and increase
  the compensation amount in the agreement, as modified by Amendments No. 1, 2,
  and 3, by an additional $15,360; approve Amendment No. 1 to the professional
  design services agreement with Kelly Sutherlin McLeod Architecture, Inc., increasing
  the total compensation amount by $21,480; approve amendment No. 1 to the
  professional services agreement with Griffin Structures increasing the total contract
  amount by $65,000; authorize the procurement of additional hazardous materials
  abatement services from Vista Environmental in the amount of $39,672; and award a
  professional design services agreement in an amount not to exceed $275,000 to CSI
  Fullmer for the design and procurement of furniture, fixtures, and equipment for the
  San Marino Center.”

  CONSENT CALENDAR

7.  RECEIVE AND FILE MONTHLY DISBURSEMENTS REPORT FOR APRIL
  2023
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file the Monthly
  Disbursements Report for the month of April 2023. If the City Council concurs with
  staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be: “I move to receive and file
  the Monthly Disbursements Report for the month of April 2023.”

8.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the April 2023 minutes. If
  the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would
  be: “I move to approve the minutes of the special meeting of April 12, 2023, the
  regular meeting of April 12, 2023, the special meeting of April 19, 2023, the
  adjourned regular meeting of April 21, 2023, the special meeting of April 21, 2023,
  the special meeting of April 26, 2023, and the adjourned regular meeting of April 28,
  2023.”

9.  APPROVAL OF RESOLUTION NO. R­23­10, ADOPTING THE CITY OF
  SAN MARINO 2023 INVESTMENT POLICY
  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve the City’s
  Investment Policy for 2023. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation,
  an appropriate motion would be: “I move to adopt Resolution No. R­23­10, a
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of San Marino, California, Adopting the 2023
  Investment Policy.”

10.  APPROVAL OF RESOLUTION NO. R­23­14, ADOPTING A LIST OF
  STREET PROJECTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023­24 FUNDED BY SB1, THE
  ROAD REPAIR AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve Resolution No. R­23­
  14, adopting a list of street projects for fiscal year 2023­24 funded by SB1. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be: “I
  move to approve Resolution No. R­23­14 adopting a list of Fiscal Year 2023­24
  projects to be funded by SB1 Road Maintenance and Rehabilitation Account Funds.”

11.  APPROVAL OF AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 2 WITH DUDEK FOR
  PROFESSIONAL DESIGN SERVICES FOR THE LIFT STATION
  IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM IN THE AMOUNT OF $47,100 AND
  EXTENDING THE TERM THROUGH DECEMBER 31, 2023
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve Amendment No. 2
  increasing the compensation amount by $47,100 and extending the term of the
  Professional Design Services Agreement through December 31, 2023. If the City
  Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be: “I
  move to approve Amendment No. 2 to the professional design services agreement
  with Dudek, increasing the compensation amount by $47,100 and extend the
  agreement through December 31, 2023, for their continued services for the Lift
  Station Improvement Program, and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  amendment on behalf of the City.”

12.  ACCEPTANCE OF 2018 POLARIS GEM E2 GOLF CART FROM ED
  MNOIAN
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council accept the donation of a 2018
  Polaris GEM e2 Golf Cart from Ed Mnoian. If the City Council concurs with Staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be: “I move to accept the donation of
  a 2018 Polaris GEM e2 Golf Cart from Ed Mnoian.”

  CLOSED SESSION

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San
Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
Marino, California 91108, and will also be included in the public agenda packet that will
available for review at the City Council meeting.
